key_insight: InfiniteWeb automatically synthesizes large, realistic, multi-page web environments so GUI agents can be trained at scale, overcoming the single-page limitations of prior LLM-based generation.
problem_solved: Addresses the shortage of diverse, functional, and interconnected web environments for training and evaluating GUI agents—manual creation is slow and single-page LLM outputs lack site-level consistency and functionality.
method: Hierarchical site synthesis: use LLMs to draft page content and structure, then programmatically generate DOM/layout and navigation to form coherent multi-page sites.
Automated validation and instrumentation: run interaction tests and constraint checks to ensure pages are functional, stateful, and link correctly for agent use.
Scalable diversification: apply templates, parameterized components, and controlled randomization to produce many varied, realistic websites and export standardized environment APIs for training.
impact: Enables large-scale, realistic training data for GUI agents, reducing dataset bottlenecks and improving agent robustness and generalization across real-world web tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: LLM generation → DOM/layout renderer → validator/test harness → environment API for agent training
Site map graphic showing multiple interconnected pages and navigation flows (before: single page; after: multi-page site)
Interaction trace example: recorded agent action sequence over a synthesized site (clicks, inputs, state changes)
Bar chart or icon showing scale: number of generated sites/environments vs. typical hand-crafted dataset size
paper_title: InfiniteWeb: Scalable Web Environment Synthesis for GUI Agent Training
paper_authors: Ziyun Zhang, Zezhou Wang, Xiaoyi Zhang, Zongyu Guo, Jiahao Li
